historical_implementation: Initial GC policy implementation; deferral returned TLAB reservations when armed.

observed_summary.notes: Short allocation probe; timings include normal runtime effect checking. Idle time includes the fixed timer wait. No RSS or production latency guarantee.

limitations: Historical three-pair measurement with CLI 3272d9bfbc59852003c6a39463f3adb0615e0eab9922df3646e90f70fc285224; subsequent runtime optimizations are not represented.
The identical optimized tracing executable was used for all six native processes; four warmup frames preceded twenty measured frames per process.
Checksums, including every measured frame, matched the official Dart 3.6.2 VM baseline.
The synthetic workload allocates objects, maps and typed buffers; it does not measure actual HTTP, JSON parsing, rendering or production latency.
Normal runtime effect checking was enabled. No stress collection or custom young-heap threshold was used.
Idle times include an identical fixed timer wait and do not isolate collector pause durations.
The measurement alternated baseline then deferred processes; CPU frequency and background load were not isolated.
Deferral removed observed in-frame collections but the summed measured frame time increased 10.2%; no speedup or smoother-frame guarantee is demonstrated.
TLAB behavior is a possible tradeoff, not a causally proven explanation of these short measurements.
No process RSS, native heap peak or production performance guarantee was measured.
The first preparation attempt failed due to missing LLVM linker selection and created no successful executable; the final successful build selected LLVM 22 explicitly.
